# Globlin

> A tray app for Windows and macOS, in beta, that watches your globally installed packages across fifteen package managers — npm, bun, pnpm, yarn, pipx, uv, cargo, go, dotnet, gem, Homebrew, scoop, winget, choco and the PowerShell Gallery — and tells you the moment one falls behind. One window with filters and bulk updates, an installer or a portable .exe on Windows (x64 and ARM64), an Apple Silicon app on macOS, free and open source under GPL-3.0.

Global command-line tools installed with `npm install -g`, `bun add -g`, `pnpm add -g` or `yarn global add` go stale silently — nothing tells you a CLI is six versions behind until a command breaks. Globlin sits in the Windows tray or the macOS menu bar, checks on a schedule (every six hours by default), and opens a window listing every global package with its source, filterable by status or by package manager and searchable by name. Clicking a row updates that package; ticking several and pressing Update selected runs them as a queue.

It never updates a package on its own. It can update itself unattended, but that setting is off by default and every download is verified against a published SHA-256 checksum before anything is replaced. Packages can be ignored, and an ignored package still shows its version but is never checked or notified about. A desktop notification fires only when the set of outdated packages changes.

Fifteen sources are supported. npm, bun, pnpm, yarn, pipx, uv, cargo, go, dotnet, gem and Homebrew are checked by default, plus scoop on Windows; the PowerShell Gallery, winget and choco are switched off by default. npm-family packages are compared against registry.npmjs.org, pipx against PyPI, cargo against crates.io, dotnet against NuGet; uv, scoop, go, gem and Homebrew report their own available versions. winget and choco are read-only: both require an elevated process to upgrade anything and Globlin runs unelevated, so it tells you and leaves the doing to you. yarn means yarn classic (v1), because yarn 2+ removed global installs.

Globlin needs no runtime of its own — it drives whatever package managers are already installed. On Windows the window is drawn by the WebView2 runtime that ships with Windows 11 and current Windows 10; the installer installs per user without elevation, and the portable exe keeps its configuration in `globlin.json` next to itself. On macOS (11 or later, Apple Silicon) Globlin.app lives in the menu bar; it is signed ad hoc rather than notarised, so the first launch has to be allowed under System Settings, Privacy and Security. There is no Linux build yet; deb and rpm packages are planned. Everything is in beta.

## Download

- [Latest release](https://github.com/TOR968/Globlin/releases/latest): `globlin-setup-x64.exe` and `globlin-setup-arm64.exe` (installer), `globlin.exe` and `globlin-arm64.exe` (portable), `Globlin-macos-arm64.zip` (macOS), each with its `.sha256`
- [All releases](https://github.com/TOR968/Globlin/releases)

## Support

Globlin is free and stays free; there is no paid tier and no telemetry.

- [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/c/TOR968): support the author's work
